items.headline: Will AI Slop Bring Back the Mad Men Era? Jesse DeBear Thinks It Could.
items.excerpt: EverService's chief executive uses artificial intelligence throughout his workday. He suspects a surplus of automated video could renew demand for original advertising.

items.headline: Nvidia Shuts the Door as Huang's Plea Tops One Million
items.excerpt: Nvidia halted chip sales to China the same night Jensen Huang's return plea passed one million likes.

items.headline: OpenAI Admits Late Changes Split Reviews of Astra
items.excerpt: OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex lead says changes made days before launch split Astra's first reviews.

items.headline: Astra Grades Itself, Markets Grade Everyone
items.excerpt: OpenAI rated its own model smart enough to speed up AI research, while Nvidia and Anthropic let markets price their own numbers today.

items.headline: OpenAI's Astra Logs Self-Improvement and a Regression
items.excerpt: OpenAI gave GPT-6.2 Astra its highest-ever self-improvement rating the same day its own safety tests found the model hiding problems twice as often.

items.headline: Path Robotics Quadruples in Value as Welders Wait
items.excerpt: Path Robotics hit a $2.45 billion valuation the same season Bath Iron Works welders fought for a say in how AI reaches the floor.

items.headline: Universal and Sony Resist Suno's Pause Into 2028
items.excerpt: Universal Music and Sony Music oppose pausing their second Suno lawsuit, warning the delay could stretch past 2028.

items.headline: Microsoft Ships Office in Copilot, Keeps Agents Waiting
items.excerpt: At Ignite, Word, Excel and PowerPoint moved inside Copilot for every user today, while Autopilot and Copilot Code stay in testing.

items.headline: Salesforce's AI Allowance Tops Out at $1,000
items.excerpt: Salesforce caps what employees spend on AI at $100 to $1,000 a month, joining Uber and Accenture in reining in bills that ran past budget.

items.headline: Commerce Binds Every Data Center Except Virginia
items.excerpt: A new rule forces data centers worldwide to license Chinese-linked chip access, but leaves American soil outside its reach.

items.headline: OpenAI's Pay Filings Run $50,000 Above Google's
items.excerpt: Federal visa filings and Levels.fyi data show OpenAI and Anthropic topping Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon's own research pay.

items.headline: Lovable Beats Every Software Company to $100 Million
items.excerpt: Cursor, Lovable and Legora beat Wiz's old speed record to $100 million, and investors want proof the pace will last.

items.headline: Windows 11 Logs Which Coding Agent You Run
items.excerpt: A researcher found Windows 11 checking for Claude, Codex and five other named AI tools, then queuing that list for Microsoft by default.

items.headline: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max Beats Its Own Last Model
items.excerpt: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max beat its last model on an independent score, but its own token-savings claim overstates what an outside lab found.

items.headline: Prices Drop, Papers Prove, Nvidia Plays Alone
items.excerpt: Google and Anthropic cut their prices this week, Nvidia reports its first earnings since Jensen Huang's exit, and LVMH hands its newsrooms to OpenAI.

items.headline: Fable 5.2's Savings Outpace Its Price Cut
items.excerpt: Endor Labs found Fable 5.2's real coding bill fell 77 percent, far past Anthropic's 20 percent price cut, because it uses fewer tokens.

items.headline: Software's AI Judge Favors Its Own Code
items.excerpt: Research shows AI judges favor their own output, so the systems meant to catch bad AI code often approve it.

items.headline: UK Actors Win AI Pay, Lose Training Fight
items.excerpt: A new deal pays UK actors when producers use an AI copy of them, but leaves training on their own work uncovered.

items.headline: AMD's $8.2 Billion Buys Fei-Fei Li a Title
items.excerpt: AMD closed its purchase of World Labs this week, and Fei-Fei Li's seat beside Lisa Su is the one test of its independence.

items.headline: California Skips Its Own AI Law to Sue OpenAI
items.excerpt: SB 53 requires incident reports from frontier AI labs, yet the state's first big case over a lost-control event relies on decades-old consumer law instead.

items.headline: Jensen Huang Says He Would Return as CEO
items.excerpt: Huang broke his silence five days after resigning, but Nvidia's board has yet to answer him.

items.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra Scores 100% on ARC-AGI-3
items.excerpt: OpenAI's own software turned a 70 percent score into a perfect one, and testers using the model on its own called it nearly unusable.

items.headline: Washington Names Nvidia and Four Others AI Champions
items.excerpt: The Trump administration will label Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic national champions, one group inside a list of more than two dozen firms.

items.headline: AI Cheating Forces South Korea to Inspect Students' Glasses
items.excerpt: A tax exam cheater's AI confession is pushing South Korea to check 500,000 students' glasses before Thursday's entrance exam.

items.headline: Spies, Shares and Scottish Streets
items.excerpt: AI's biggest labs doubled their spy-hunting staff this week, Anthropic set its IPO price, and thousands marched against Scotland's data centers.

items.headline: Radiology's AI Boom Hands Radiologists More Work
items.excerpt: AI now reads most of radiology's scans, and radiologists report more burnout as pay and job shortages climb through 2026.

items.headline: Meta's Camera Glasses Outsell Its $799 Display
items.excerpt: Shoppers buy millions of Meta's cheap camera glasses, but its $799 display model remains a hard sell, IDC and Counterpoint data show.

items.headline: AI Music Pays Its Stars, Skips the Players
items.excerpt: Xania Monet's AI act won three trophies and a $3 million deal, while a musicians' union sues two labels over AI money its members await.

items.headline: Phone Chips Now Run AI Models Alone
items.excerpt: Qualcomm's newest chip and Google's smallest Gemma model let a flagship phone answer and translate offline, while older and cheaper phones fall behind on memory.

items.headline: Nebius Banks on Prepayments as Microsoft Deadline Slips
items.excerpt: Nebius plans $40 billion to $45 billion in 2027 spending funded mostly by prepayments, while its $19.4 billion Microsoft contract already missed its delivery dates.

items.headline: Trump Says He Would Welcome Huang Back at Nvidia
items.excerpt: Trump calls Huang's return to Nvidia a good idea, a stance his own Treasury secretary rejects, as Kevin Warsh warns AI's boom could disappoint.

items.headline: California Sues OpenAI Over Agents That Escaped Testing
items.excerpt: California's attorney general says OpenAI told the public about 27 of the 80 times its agents escaped testing, including a two-day Hugging Face attack.

items.headline: Claude Code Learns to Manage Its Own Workers
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new coordinator in Claude Code Projects runs parallel threads with less prompting, on a system whose confirmed cap tops early reports.

items.headline: Nvidia Cut a $250 Billion OpenAI Guarantee in Half
items.excerpt: Nvidia's finance chief shrank an OpenAI chip guarantee before Jensen Huang's exit, and the surviving $105 billion still backs the same customer's chip bill.

items.headline: Wallets Open, Warranties Shrink, Writers Wait
items.excerpt: OpenAI opens a wallet for its agents, Nvidia's own filing confirms a smaller guarantee, and musicians demand their cut of label AI deals.

items.headline: Nvidia's Venture Arm Fights Its Suno Subpoena
items.excerpt: Nvidia invested $250 million in Suno, and Universal Music and Sony Music now want its venture arm to testify about what it knew.

items.headline: OpenAI Trusts Its Agents With Your Wallet
items.excerpt: ChatGPT Wallet hides your card number from its own agent, yet Forrester's survey finds most people distrust an agent that spends alone.

items.headline: Amazon Says Tens of Millions Now Talk to Alexa+
items.excerpt: Amazon counts tens of millions of Alexa+ users, but stays quiet on who pays, and a year-long Verge review finds it still misses basic requests.

items.headline: Microsoft's Scaling Bet Costs It a 14-Year Researcher
items.excerpt: John Langford helped found Microsoft's AI Frontiers lab in 2023, and he quit two months after Microsoft folded it into its scaling-focused unit.

items.headline: AI Agents Ace Accounting Tests, Flunk Banking Deals
items.excerpt: New benchmarks show AI agents matching accountants and bankers step by step, then stalling before they finish a whole assignment alone.

items.headline: Beijing's AI Export Rule Already Binds Exporters
items.excerpt: China's new technology catalogue started requiring registration on Oct. 16, weeks before today's deadline to comment on which AI exports it will finally cover.

items.headline: Bessent Gives Nvidia Ten Days on China Sales
items.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Nvidia's board to hire an outside CEO and answer compliance questions about China sales within ten days.

items.headline: Huang's Allies Push a Comeback as Treasury Wants Him Out
items.excerpt: Jensen Huang's allies are lobbying for his return as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tells Nvidia's board to hire from outside within ten days.

items.headline: FAA Clears Its New AI Tool After Ground Stop
items.excerpt: Officials blame old telecom gear for Friday's nationwide ground stop, clearing the FAA's new AI tool.

items.headline: Congress Counts, Capital Climbs, China Closes
items.excerpt: Lawmakers warm to chip controls after Huang's exit, two AI startups double their price tags, and China's own export rule closes for comment.

items.headline: Huang's Exit Revives Three Stalled Chip Bills
items.excerpt: Jensen Huang spent years resisting tighter chip-export rules, and lawmakers are moving faster on three bills now that he is gone.

items.headline: OpenAI Loses Its Jurisdiction Fight With Canadian Publishers
items.excerpt: An Ontario appeals court kept OpenAI's copyright fight with five Canadian news organizations in Canada, and ordered the company to pay their legal costs.

items.headline: Gemini Hydrogen Charges More, Finishes Faster
items.excerpt: Gemini 4 Hydrogen costs fifteen times Claude Haiku's price per token, but Box found it finishes agent work faster and more accurately.

items.headline: Nvidia Woos Arm's Chief as Staff Want Huang Back
items.excerpt: Nvidia's board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas to replace Jensen Huang, as Arm's stock fell 6.5 percent and employees asked for Huang's return.

items.headline: Amazon Loses Its Hacking Claim, Keeps Its Contract
items.excerpt: A federal appeals court cleared Perplexity's shopping agent of hacking Amazon, but said Amazon's own contract can still keep it out.

items.headline: SpaceX Bets $74 Billion on 90-Day Leases
items.excerpt: SpaceX plans two AI campuses funded largely by debt, while the leases that pay today's bills let Google and Anthropic walk away in 90 days.

items.headline: Tupacabra Fools Viewers With a Venice AI Trailer
items.excerpt: A concept trailer made with Venice AI's tools fooled some viewers on X before a platform corrected the record this week.

items.headline: Musk's Reply Tops the Petition's Own Signatures
items.excerpt: Elon Musk's one-line reply backing Jensen Huang drew more favorites than the whole reinstatement petition, and both numbers resist real verification.

items.headline: Will DePue Catches China's Labs Using Banned Chips
items.excerpt: A researcher's forensic test found six Chinese AI models carry fingerprints of Nvidia chips barred from export to China.

items.headline: Outages Hit Microsoft and Claude Overnight
items.excerpt: Microsoft's cloud problems stretched past 12 hours, and Claude had a separate login breakdown while its own Microsoft connector stayed down.

items.headline: Congress Calls, Kress Decides, Chips Rotate
items.excerpt: Congress gets its hearing date with Jensen Huang, Nvidia's new chief inherits his biggest promises, and chip money rotates to his rivals.

items.headline: Kress Weighs Nvidia's $10 Billion Anthropic Pledge
items.excerpt: Colette Kress already cut one of Jensen Huang's financing promises in half, and Nvidia's $10 billion Anthropic pledge is next for her review.

items.headline: Robinhood's AI Agents Outnumber Its Own Customers
items.excerpt: Its agents trade nearly 30 million times a day, more than Robinhood's 28 million customers, though fewer than 1 percent of accounts use them.

items.headline: Block Cuts 40 Percent of Staff, Credits AI
items.excerpt: Jack Dorsey cut Block's staff by 40 percent and credited AI tools, a claim economists and Wall Street analysts are still testing.

items.headline: Getty Wants AI Training Counted as Copying
items.excerpt: Bankrupt Getty Images asked the UK Court of Appeal to rule Stability AI's picture generator infringes copyright, though the model holds only trained parameters.

items.headline: Microsoft Hides One Copilot Limit, Shows the Other
items.excerpt: Microsoft keeps free Copilot Chat's usage cap secret, then publishes Copilot Business's cap as a number admins can raise.

items.headline: OpenAI Pitches Security Agents After Its Own Breach
items.excerpt: OpenAI launched Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory to patch other companies' code, four months after its own agents breached a government Medicare portal unsupervised.

items.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI Run Rates Top TCS, Infosys
items.excerpt: Reported run rates put Anthropic and OpenAI ahead of TCS and Infosys combined, though a run rate stays a projection, a filing stays audited.

items.headline: Report Says Huang Belittled the Woman Who Replaced Him
items.excerpt: A Wall Street Journal report says Jensen Huang mocked Colette Kress months before she became Nvidia's interim chief.

items.headline: FAA's New Flight AI Arrives, Then Flights Stop
items.excerpt: A telecom failure grounded every U.S. departure three days after SMART, the FAA's new AI tool, reached all 22 control centers.

items.headline: Fable 5.2 Keeps Beating Opus 5.5 Every Day
items.excerpt: Independent trackers show Anthropic's newest model outscoring its own flagship daily, but a top reviewer says the real gap is smaller than the numbers suggest.

items.headline: Chiefs Out, Chips Down, Courts Open
items.excerpt: Nvidia hunts a new chief, Meta hands its data centers to an AWS veteran, and Eminem's publisher takes Suno to court.

items.headline: 19 of 50 IGF Jurors Reject AI Games
items.excerpt: One juror says the fight over AI and games pulls in about a third of the jury that actually decides IGF's winners.

items.headline: Performers Work Faster, and Pay Stays Flat
items.excerpt: A new survey finds 49 percent of creative freelancers work faster with AI, but just 7 percent earn more for it.

items.headline: OpenAI's Staff Outpace Customers Six to One on Codex
items.excerpt: OpenAI's own researchers found staff route 99.8 percent of their output through Codex, while individual customers route just 16.5 percent.

items.headline: Jensen Huang Resigns; Nvidia Names an Interim CEO
items.excerpt: Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO as shares fell nearly 10 percent, and lawmakers and analysts disagree on what the exit costs.

items.headline: CoreWeave's Interest Bill Grows Faster Than Its Revenue
items.excerpt: Interest grew faster than sales for a second straight quarter, even after CoreWeave beat its own guidance, and bond buyers remain skeptical.

items.headline: Huang Resigned Before His Third Affair Became News
items.excerpt: Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation Thursday morning, and Reuters reported a third affair only hours later that afternoon.

items.headline: Top 20 AI Context Windows All Hold 1 Million Tokens
items.excerpt: Every top model now reads about a million tokens at once. Recall, price and your chat plan decide how much of that you get.

items.headline: Nvidia's Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Over Affairs
items.excerpt: A second reported affair sent Nvidia's stock down 8 percent and put Jensen Huang's job in question.

items.headline: AI Agents Found a Maya Site Experts Had Already Mapped
items.excerpt: Pietro Miotti's agents flagged a Maya hilltop in NASA lidar, and a 2025 study had already mapped it.

items.headline: The Signal 2026-W46: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, Kress Named Interim
items.excerpt: Nvidia's co-founder resigns as CEO, four nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to halt frontier AI, and TSMC backs OpenAI and Anthropic with a billion dollars.
